key_insight: The paper uses control barrier functions to keep grid-forming photovoltaic converters within safe voltage and current limits while preserving stable AC voltage and frequency control.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical way to make PV inverters more fault-tolerant and grid-supportive without violating device constraints during irradiance changes, load steps, or grid faults.
method: Start with unconstrained dual-port grid-forming control for the PV inverter.
Add control barrier functions to encode AC/DC voltage and current safety limits.
Use real-time optimization to minimally adjust the control action whenever constraints are at risk.
evidence_signal: The approach is evaluated in electromagnetic transient simulations in MATLAB/Simulink under grid faults, irradiance changes, and load perturbations.
watch_item: Real-time optimization adds implementation complexity and may be challenging to guarantee fast enough responses on embedded inverter hardware.
paper_title: Constrained Grid-Forming Control for Photovoltaic Systems: A Control Barrier Function Approach
